Subject: Re: Initial MAP: POC access & infra playbook — API keys, org setup, allowlist, VPC peering

Thanks Karthik — excited to kick off. We want the POC to be as close to production as possible; key asks from our side:
- API keys scoped to the POC org, separate from prod keys
- IP allowlist for our ingestion endpoints and the admin console
- VPC peering for low-latency model calls (we run on GCP us-central1)
- A one-week test window followed by a go/no-go decision and a small pilot if green

Can you send a short playbook we can share with our security and network folks? Ben and our IT Ops are looped.

Thanks,

Head of Data Integrations
VectorMed

Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Initial MAP: POC access & infra playbook — API keys, org setup, allowlist, VPC peering

Hi Alice — great to see alignment. Draft MAP/playbook attached — it breaks the POC into discrete ownerable tasks and timing. Summary of what’s in the doc: 
1) Org & API access (owner: Karthik) — Create a POC Redwood org, generate scoped API keys, and rotate keys at the handover. Expected completion: 2 business days after agreement.
2) Network controls (owner: VectorMed IT + Redwood network lead) — Provide IP ranges for allowlist; we will validate connectivity to the runtime endpoints.
3) VPC peering (owner: VectorMed cloud team + Redwood infra) — Exchange VPC project ids, proposed subnets, and peer config. Redwood supports GCP peering in us-central1; expected setup time 5–7 business days depending on approvals.
4) Pilot traffic plan & success criteria (owner: VectorMed product + Redwood CS) — Defined test payloads, latency targets, and data retention expectations.

Next steps I propose:
- VectorMed to share current IP ranges and a contact for VPC peering (if you want, jared@cloudconnect can help coordinate).
- We provision a scoped API key and post the key to the POC org.
- Joint connectivity test scheduled for Aug 24 — tentative.

I attached: redwood_map_v1.pdf (playbook) and vpc-peering-reqs.docx (template).

Can the VectorMed IT team confirm the IP ranges and a preferred date/time for the connectivity test?

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1-415-555-0134

Attachments: redwood_map_v1.pdf (pdf stub), vpc-peering-reqs.docx (docx stub)

Subject: Re: Initial MAP: POC access & infra playbook — API keys, org setup, allowlist, VPC peering

Thanks for the details IT Ops — happy to be the technical lead for Redwood on the VPC peering. Quick operational notes from our infra side: 
- Redwood will create a POC org and a scoped API key with the following perms: model inference read/write for the POC project only; no billing admin privileges. Key will be shared via DocuSign secure transfer link after VectorMed accepts the MAP.
- For peering we need: project-id, vpc-name, subnet CIDRs, and a contact with GCP console access. Please send those to me and Jared and we’ll open the request.
- We will run an automated connectivity and TLS handshake test during the Aug 24 window; post-test we’ll document latency and token counts.

Action items captured here (from our side):
- laura_bennett: initiate Redwood peering request and preflight checks (ETA: Aug 20)
- rishi_malhotra: generate scoped API key and schedule rotation policy in the MAP (ETA: Aug 19)
- marissa_cole: draft the go/no-go criteria and success metrics doc (ETA: Aug 21)

If Aug 24 10:00am PT works for VectorMed, I’ll block calendar and share the test play.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
